videos.t: Power Glove MIDI Controller Demo
videos.desc:
Quick Demo of the Power Glove MIDI Controller I built.

I basically smashed the Power Glove project below together with the excellent NES Library to get the controller working as well. I used the MIDI USB Library and a Pro-Micro board to make mine a wired version of the project.

Unfortunately it only captures the standard controller buttons, so the Numpad isn't usable without creating a custom PCB to directly wire into the Arduino. Maybe I'll get around to that someday?

Maybe if there's interest I'll put together a full blown tutorial. Thanks for watching!

Lonks:
https://learn.adafruit.com/

videos.t: MSXey Synth Demo
videos.desc:
I'm calling this synth MSXey mostly because that's easier to say than "The AY-3-8910 (YM2149) Synth from TheSpodShed's Excellent Instructable" and because I think I'm clever since the chip was used in the MSX2. I know I'm clever because I explained my own joke.

If you want to build one, the Instructable is here:
https://www.instructables.com/id/Arduino-MIDI-Chiptune-Synthesizer/

I designed the PCB because a) I am very bad at soldering and b) I wanted to learn how. And shockingly the first attempt actually worked!

Oh yeah and the song is Vampire Killer.

videos.t: Hamberder Soundscape Mangler Demo
videos.desc:
Hamberder Soundscape Mangler!

This was a bit of a failed experiment, since what I was going for was closer to a pedal than this turned out. It reacts wildly different to input levels and works best between two sources of amplification (a hot signal off a synth and a mixer pre in this case).

Don't think I'll make a regular product of it, but seems like a fun niche device, and it's pretty fun if wildly impractical.
